Ntwine — parametric grid

144 options. Variants of one construction: a single contiguous stroke, two blobs, and exact 180° rotational symmetry. Quote an id and I'll take it further.

What varies

blob w × hsize and shape of each swoop
tilteach blob's own rotation
axisdirection from the centre to the blob — the letter's lean
disthow far the blobs sit from the centre
wraphow far round the blob the stroke travels
side / dirwhere the line originates on the blob, and which way round
tailterminal length

The 144 options

Two crossings, verified on every variant. The count is checked at the same sampling density as the final report — a coarser check is not a weaker check but a different one, and an optimiser will find the gap between them. It did, once: a shape with five crossings passed a coarse test as two.

Symmetry is exact, not approximate. Each half is authored once and the other half is its 180° rotation, so the two can't drift. Measured on the point set, the worst deviation across all 144 is 1.27e-13 units — floating-point noise. That is a proof, not a pixel comparison.

Nothing here grazes. The stroke meets a blob at a computed tangent point, so joins have no kink, and the two stems form one straight line through the centre rather than a pile-up. Any combination where two parts of the stroke ran closer than 1.7 stroke-widths at under 24° to each other was discarded — that near-parallel graze is what reads as a smudge. Combinations with no crossing (not a letterform) or more than three (a scribble) were dropped too: 8640 combinations became 2815 clean, 657 visually distinct, and these 144.

Not yet decided: weight, colour and whether the tile stays. Everything is drawn at a uniform 22-unit stroke purely so the shapes compare fairly.
